finding.claim: The ban endpoint's admin check is not enforced. require_admin() calls abort(403), which raises an HTTPException. The surrounding `except Exception` catches it, logs a warning and continues to do_ban(uid). Any authenticated non-admin user can therefore ban arbitrary users. The unban route has no try/except and is correctly protected.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban, with an attacker-chosen uid in the URL.

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban is registered with no decorator or middleware guard.
require_admin(g.user) is called; for a non-admin user it calls abort(403) (lines 10-11), raising an HTTPException.
`except Exception` catches the HTTPException (a subclass of Exception).
The handler only logs a warning and does not re-raise or return.
Execution falls through to do_ban(uid) and returns ok=True.

finding.guards_checked: require_admin is the only guard, and the try/except nullifies it. There is no other middleware, before_request hook or decorator in the file. The unban route (line 26) calls require_admin without a try/except, so it is enforced. The log line also writes the user's name, which is minor.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403, but the bare `except Exception` at admin.py:18 swallows it. No decorator, before_request hook or middleware exists in the file.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:17-20, abort(403) raises an HTTPException that `except Exception` catches and only logs, so do_ban(uid) at line 20 runs for any authenticated non-admin, whereas unban (admin.py:26) is unguarded by try/except and so is enforced.
